For the Petitioner : Mr. Mahesh Kumar Sinha, Adv.

For the Respondents : Mr. Niraj Kumar Mishra,
A.C to G.P.IV : Mr. Rajesh Lala, Advocate ----
th 06/Dated: 08 April, 2024 1.
Heard the parties.

2. The present writ petition has been filed for following reliefs:-
"For direction upon the respondents specially respondent Nos.1 to 4 and directing them not to create any obstruction to the petitioner in construction of house over the Plot No.76/19, Area 03 Katha, Jamabandi No.28 of Village-Lalmatia as because the said land is ancestral land of the petitioner which was acquire by the grandfather of the petitioner namely, Hari Shankar Goswami through settlement order dated 28/04/1952 (Annexure-1) passed in Damin Settlement Case No.15/1949-50, passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer, Godda, District Santhal Parganas and delivery of possession over the said land has been taken by the grandfather of the petitioner through due process on 09/12/1952 (Annexure-3) and in this regard Kanoongo has submitted his report dated 25/03/1953 (Annexure-4) and petitioner further prays that to direct the respondent Nos.1 to 4 not take any coercive steps against the petitioner without initiating any proceeding in accordance with law and without issuing any notice against him and further prays for a direction upon the respondents and directing them not to start construction work of Marriage Hall over the petitioner's land."
3. It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the description of the land is as follows:-
"Plot No.76/19, Area 03 Katha, Jamabandi No.28 of Village-Lalmatia"
4. The claim of the petitioner is on the basis of inheritance, claiming that the said land is the ancestral property of the petitioner.
It has been submitted that he still has the possession over the said land, but the respondents are not allowing the petitioner to make any construction on the said piece of land.
The writ petition has been filed for restraining the respondents from interfering with the possession of the petitioner.
The petitioner has further made a complaint that the 'Marriage Hall' is being constructed by the respondents in the said piece of land, which is per se illegal.

5. Learned counsel for the respondents have opposed the prayer of the petitioner and it has been submitted that the land, in question, has already been acquired by Rajmahal Area of Eastern Coalfields Limited under CBA (A&D) Act, 1957 vide S.O. No.28(E) in the year 1981 and published in Gazette Notification No.19(26)/80-CL.

sentences.text:
Paragraph No.9 of the counter affidavit filed by the respondent No.3 is quoted herein below:-
"9.

That on perusal of the relevant record it is revealed that upon acquisition of the said land, Shri Badrinath Goswami [Son of Late Hari Shankar Goswami] i.e, father of the writ petitioner was ordered to be paid a sum of Rs.1,755.28 against plot No.76/19 [inadvertently typed as Plot No.76/18 in payment receipt] for an Area of 3 Katha in Lalmatia Mouja.

The same can be cross checked from the petitioners' document itself in Annexure-2 [Item No.19 in Page No.20] May it be mentioned that all the persons who were entitled to receive the compensation in Plot No.76 in Mouza-Lalmatia has already received the compensation.
No complaint with regard to wrong distribution or non-payment of the compensation amount has been received till date.

Thus, in the fact and circumstances the petitioner has made false statement before this Hon'ble Court and has made wrong claim of compensation for the land in question."
7.
On the above basis, it has been submitted that the land, in question, is an acquired property and as such, the respondents have every right to make construction.

8. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and from perusal of the records, it appears that there was an acquisition proceedings and the land, in question, has vested to the respondents by operation of law.

There is material to suggest that the compensation has already been paid to the petitioner.
9.
In that view of the matter, this Court finds no reason to entertain the present writ petition.
Accordingly, it is hereby, disposed of giving liberty to the petitioner to work out his remedy in accordance with law.

(Rajesh Kumar, J.) Raja/-
